title: The Apology of David
author: P. Kyle McCarter Jr.
allowedUseNotes: Modern copyrighted peer-reviewed journal article. Project stores only its own summary/paraphrase of the article's thesis and scope, no reproduction of McCarter's own text.
summary: McCarter's foundational article proposing that the narrative running from roughly 1 Samuel 16 through 2 Samuel 5 ("the History of David's Rise") is best read as a work of political apologetic — a composition answering specific, nameable charges against David's legitimacy by showing, episode by episode, that he was not responsible for the deaths that cleared his path to the throne: Nabal, Saul and Jonathan, Abner, and Ish-bosheth. McCarter reads 2 Samuel 3's insistence that Abner's death was Joab's doing and not David's will (3:26b, 28-30, 36-37) and 2 Samuel 4's parallel insistence regarding Ish-bosheth's assassination (David's retelling of the Ziklag execution at 4:9-10, the execution of Rechab and Baanah at 4:12) as belonging to this same defensive pattern, coining the phrase "the apology of David" for the genre. This project cites the article specifically for that literary-critical reading — that a named, influential, peer-reviewed critical study treats the narrative's repeated insistence on David's innocence as apologetic shaping rather than incidental reporting — as one clearly labeled scholarlyView (view-public-response-apologia) alongside, not replacing, a plain-report reading that treats the same verses as straightforward narration.
confidenceNotes: Bibliographic details (journal, volume/issue, page range 489-504, 1980) are corroborated across multiple independent secondary/tertiary sources describing and citing this article by name (including the Journal of Biblical Literature's own Scholarly Publishing Collective listing and multiple academic papers and reviews citing it as the origin of the 'apology of David' reading), not from direct page-by-page inspection of the original JBL issue, which was not accessible in this pass.
